title: Herald REST API contract reference
description: Canonical record for a Herald REST API surface — the routes, request/response shapes, status codes, and behavioral contracts a client depends on. One record per cohesive API family. The same facts feed the API-reference page, the OpenAPI doc, the SPA client's expectations, and the server implementer's checklist, so they live in a structured record rather than free-form markdown. Prose explanation (the 'why this shape' narrative) lives in prose/<repo>/reference/; this record carries the queryable surface.

id.description: Stable identifier for the API family, used as the record file's base name.

status.description: Maturity of the contract's IMPLEMENTATION. 'implemented-fakeserver' = the FakeServer honors the wire shape end to end; 'implemented-reference-host' = the in-memory Herald.RestApi.Host honors it; 'implemented-production' = a real pipeline-backed server honors it; 'partial'/'planned' carry the honest gap.

first-defined.description: Date the contract shape was first defined.

contract-package.description: The .NET package that owns the contract types (DTOs + interface). The wire shape is what consumers depend on; the package is where the shape is defined.

statement.description: What this API family does, in plain words.

out-of-scope.description: Operations a reader might expect here but that live elsewhere (or persist client-side only); name them so the reader does not hunt.

demo-note.description: How the demo/no-auth path satisfies the capability check, if relevant.

timing-contract.description: Read-after-write / convergence guarantees the consumer can rely on (e.g. PATCH-200 means queryable on next GET).

shared-shapes.description: DTO records reused across routes in the family. Each entry names the shape and its fields so the route table can reference by name.

section.description: Source-plan section reference (e.g. live-viewer-port-plan §3.2), when the route traces to a spec section.

request-shape.description: Name of a shared-shape, or an inline description for one-off bodies. Absent for bodyless requests.

response-shape.description: Name of a shared-shape, or an inline description.

etag.description: Optimistic-concurrency posture for the route: 'required', 'opt-in', or 'none'.

sse.description: Server-sent-event channels the family interacts with.

kind.description: The envelope kind discriminator on the wire.

consumers.description: Who depends on this contract today, and against which implementation.

implementation-gap.description: The honest state of the production implementation: which routes are backed by a real pipeline and which are mock/reference only. Names the open issue if there is one.
